title: ~5.7% of loaded articles silently drop their publish date instead of saying so
what_i_did: Loaded the Feed surface to exhaustion via repeated 'Load more' clicks (port 8012, theme=ink, lang=en, 1440x900) until all 370 eligible articles (453 total minus the stated '83 held back') were in the DOM, then scanned every .feed-card .feed-meta line for the expected 'SOURCE · DATE · LANG' shape.
what_i_saw: 21 of 370 loaded article cards (5.7%) render their meta line as 'SOURCE · LANG' — the date segment and one of its two separating middots are simply absent, e.g. 'FR Regional Herald fr · FR' next to a normal sibling card reading 'FR Regional Herald fr · 2023-01-14 · FR'. Confirmed across all 8 corpus languages and re-confirmed on a fresh session with a different random shuffle (article ids 386, 377, 276, 157, 56, 322, 221, 102, 354, 1, 134, 267, 166, 47, 299, 432, 79, 331, 212, 111, 244 all reproduce it).
evidence: /home/user/oo-ui/wf-a1/feed/feed-missing-date-zoom.png (visual: 'FR Regional Herald fr · FR', no date); /home/user/oo-ui/wf-a1/feed/feed-missing-date-context.png; raw counts in the session transcript (21/370) reproduced via direct DOM query on #feed-list .feed-meta.
why_it_matters: The project's own non-negotiable is 'degrade loudly' — every signal should carry its method/caveat, never a silent gap. title: A standalone 'NOT term' query silently returns everything instead of excluding matches — exactly the syntax the search box's own placeholder advertises
what_i_did: Queried `NOT opinion` alone (no other terms), then queried `opinion` alone to establish the exclusion set, on the corpus of 453 total articles.
what_i_saw: `opinion` alone correctly matched exactly 1 article. `NOT opinion` alone, which per the placeholder's own advertised syntax ('AND / OR / NOT') should exclude that 1 article and return 452, instead returned all 453 — i.e. the NOT operator with no preceding positive term is silently ignored rather than applied as an exclusion.
evidence: Measured counts this session: `opinion` → 1 result; `NOT opinion` → 453 results (= total corpus size, confirmed via the same session's baseline '453 result(s)' on initial load).
why_it_matters: The query box's placeholder text is `(climate OR energy) AND policy NOT opinion` — the app is actively teaching users this exact syntax. A user who tries the simpler standalone form (`NOT badterm`) to filter out noise gets no filtering at all, with no error or warning that the exclusion did not take effect — a silent violation of the honesty-by-construction principle applied to the app's own advertised query language.

title: The time-range slider's ARIA value attributes are date strings, not numbers — invalid per the ARIA slider spec (axe: critical)
what_i_did: Ran axe-core (wcag2a/aa, wcag21a/aa, best-practice) against the settled Search surface, both on initial load and after interaction.

title: The shared audit harness's contrast scanner produces false positives for any element with its own background-color
what_i_did: Ran a.contrast_failures() on the settled Feed surface (returned 3-4 'failures': a.skip-link, the active 'Shuffled' order pill, the 'Load more' button, and #net-coach-go), then read getComputedStyle() directly on each flagged element to get its OWN background-color and foreground color, and hand-computed the WCAG contrast ratio between them.

The harness instead reported ratios of 1.00-1.08 because oohelp.py's backdrop() function explicitly excludes the element itself from the ancestor chain it composites ('const anc = chain(el); anc.pop();'), so for any element that paints its own background (buttons, chips, badges, the skip-link) it tests the foreground color against the wrong (parent panel) backdrop instead of the element's own.
evidence: /home/user/oo-ui/wf-a1/feed/feed-deep-probes.json (deep_contrast, 3 entries); manual computed-style dump in session transcript: Shuffled button bg=rgb(91,157,217) color=rgb(10,15,22); Skip link bg=rgb(91,157,217) color=rgb(10,15,22) (same pair, confirmed at top:8px once focused, i.e. genuinely visible, not just an off-screen artifact).

suggestion: Have backdrop() include the element's own background-color (composited at full opacity) as the innermost layer before walking ancestors, rather than skipping it.

title: The shared contrast_failures() harness ignores an element's OWN background-color, producing false-positive 'near-1:1' failures on solid-filled buttons
affects: The shared /home/user/oo-ui/oohelp.py `backdrop()` helper used by every theme/locale/viewport agent in this audit — not specific to any one theme. Concretely inflates the raw failure counts for #net-coach-go ('Go online') and some `.tiny` action buttons ('Load more', 'Shuffled') on every dark theme, most visibly cyber (ratio reported as 1.01).
what_i_did: Noticed `#net-coach-go` and `.tiny` buttons reported near-1:1 ratios with declaredColor a near-black rgb(4,18,26)-family value against a near-black composited 'bg' — implausible for a button meant to be clickable/legible. Read oohelp.py's `backdrop(el)` function: it builds the ancestor chain then explicitly `anc.pop()`s the element itself before compositing backgrounds, so an element's OWN background-color is never included in the 'bg' the text is scored against. I then directly queried #net-coach-go's own computed background in the cyber theme.
what_i_saw: #net-coach-go's own background is `rgb(34, 211, 238)` (a bright cyan accent fill) with `color: rgb(4, 18, 26)` (near-black) — a deliberately high-contrast pairing (dark text on a bright accent button), not a defect. The harness's contrast_failures() instead scored the near-black text against the PAGE background behind the button (since it skips the button's own paint), yielding the spurious 1.01:1 'failure'. The same shape recurs for `.tiny` buttons that carry their own background.
evidence: cyber theme-cyber.json worstContrast: {'sel':'button#net-coach-go','text':'Go online','ratio':1.01,'declaredColor':'rgb(4, 18, 26)','bg':[13,17,32]}; live probe: getComputedStyle('#net-coach-go') => {background:'rgb(34, 211, 238)', color:'rgb(4, 18, 26)'}; oohelp.py's `backdrop()` function (`anc.pop()` removing `el` itself before compositing).
why_it_matters: This is a finding about the audit tooling, not the app: the raw contrastFailureCount numbers recorded across this whole matrix (and presumably every sibling agent's JSON using the same harness) systematically overstate real defects wherever a button/pill paints its own solid or semi-opaque background. Anyone downstream trusting the raw counts without re-deriving the element's own fill (as I did for F2's span.chip, which genuinely has no own background) will over-report.

suggestion: For future runs, extend the harness's backdrop() to fall back to the scanned element's own background-color/backgroundImage when it is opaque, rather than always deferring to ancestors.
